🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin holds the mid-$80Ks after a historic Q3 and a week of ETF inflows, while fallout from the $387.5M Bitget hack reignites the debate over decentralization and responsibility. 🛡️ THORChain Rejects Bitget's Plea to Block Hacker Addresses Bitget CEO Gracy Chen formally asked THORChain to refuse service to wallets tied to the exchange's $387.5M breach after attackers used the protocol to swap stolen ETH and BNB into native Bitcoin. THORChain declined, citing its permissionless design. Meanwhile, the hacker has moved about $83M in XRP that Ripple has no way to freeze. Bitget says customer balances are covered and withdrawals resume in stages from Sept. 28. Read full story ₿ Bitcoin Heads for Its Second-Best Q3 Ever as Ether Sets a Record Bitcoin has gained roughly 43.5% this quarter, climbing from about $58,500 to around $84,000 — a Q3 bested only by 2017. Ether did even better, rising about 71% for its strongest third quarter on record, supported by stronger ETF demand, rising spot volume and restrained profit-taking. More details 📈 Bitcoin ETFs Stretch Inflow Streak to Seven Days and $2.98B U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs added $134.5M on Friday, their seventh straight day of inflows, pulling in close to $3B since Sept. 17. The run marks a sharp reversal from mid-September outflows and has flipped 2026 ETF flows back into positive territory. Read more 📜 Michael Saylor Proposes a "Bill of Digital Rights" Strategy's executive chairman published an essay arguing the AI era needs digital-asset freedoms rather than restrictions: the rights to create, issue, custody, transfer and use digital assets. He also called for banks to hold and lend against Bitcoin on normal commercial terms, criticizing heavy Basel capital charges. See details ⚖️ Kalshi Loses Another Appeal as a Supreme Court Fight Looms A Sixth Circuit panel ruled that sports-related event contracts are not swaps and therefore fall under state rather than federal oversight. The loss adds to a split among appeals courts and sets up a potential Supreme Court showdown over how prediction markets are regulated in the U.S. Read full story 🏛️ SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce to Step Down on Oct. 2 Hester Peirce, the SEC's most consistent crypto advocate and head of its crypto task force, will leave the agency next week. Sleeping 
 can be harder than it looks. Although the numbers are unreliable, the best guess is that perhaps a third of adults in Western countries have trouble sleeping at least once a week. Perhaps 10% struggle enough to qualify for a medical diagnosis of insomnia. In some people sleep problems can last for years.


 Sleeping pills can help. But some cause dependence, and doctors can be wary of prescribing them for more than a few weeks.
